primary.thesis: The rules name Gemini 3.6 Flash and 3.7 Flash as existing models and say that any rollout, promotion or snapshot of 3.7 Flash does not count. That suggests 3.7 Flash is recent, and likely still in preview or only just generally available, as of 2026-08-24. Google usually leaves a Flash version out for several weeks to a few months before the next point version. It first ships the Pro tier or a preview, then Flash, and it spaces these releases out. A new 3.8+ Flash within a week is very unlikely. One within about three weeks is also unlikely, because Google would be cutting short the 3.7 Flash rollout it is still promoting. Snapshot or dated updates to 3.7 Flash (for example 3.7-flash-09-2026) are the most likely Flash news in September, and they explicitly do not qualify. Rules also exclude Flash-Lite, Image, Live, TTS and Omni variants, which take away many of the 'Flash' headlines that might otherwise resolve these contracts YES. October 31 is the date where uncertainty really starts to matter, so I stay out of C4.

basket.reason: Only about a week after the rules date. A general-access 3.8+ Flash that soon would mean Google replaces its current Flash almost as soon as it arrives, and nothing suggests a preview or leak is pending.

Three weeks is shorter than Google's usual gap between core Flash versions. Mid-September Flash news is more likely to be 3.7 Flash snapshots or GA promotion, or Flash-Lite/Image variants, and none of these qualify.

Five weeks is still short of the usual gap. Google often releases a new Pro or preview before the matching Flash, and I see no sign of a 3.8 Pro yet. A private or closed early-access test would not count either.

failure_narrative: The basket loses if Google speeds up its release pace sharply. The mechanism would be Google moving to a fast point-release cycle, as the jumps through 3.6 and 3.7 suggest it may already have done. It would then ship a 'Gemini 3.8 Flash' or 'Gemini 4 Flash' preview in AI Studio or the Gemini app before September 30, open to everyone as a public preview. Triggers could include a competitor frontier or small-model launch that takes over the benchmarks, a Google hardware or developer event (Pixel launch or a Cloud event) used as a launch stage, or 3.7 Flash having actually launched weeks earlier than I assume. An open public preview meets the 'publicly accessible' test, so even an early experimental release would resolve C1, C2 or C3 YES.
hedge_thesis: In the worlds where Google ships a 3.8+ Flash early, the usual cause is strong competitive pressure in cheap, fast models. OpenAI, Anthropic, xAI or a Chinese lab (DeepSeek, Qwen) releases a small or mid-tier model that beats the current Gemini Flash on price and performance, or tops leaderboards like LMArena. Google has historically answered those launches within weeks by bringing forward its own releases. So the hedge is that a rival lab ships a notable new small or mid-tier model, such as a GPT mini, Claude Haiku/Sonnet or DeepSeek release, in late August or September 2026. That launch is what would push Google to move early, so it tends to be true in exactly the worlds where my NO basket fails. Such a launch would also tend to show up as volatility in AI leaderboard rankings and in Alphabet's stock around announcements.
